title: The personal infinitive
objectives: I can form the personal infinitive (falares, falarmos, falarem) for regular and irregular verbs.
I can decide when the infinitive needs its own ending because its subject differs from the main verb.
I can use the personal infinitive after prepositions such as antes de, depois de, sem, para, por and ao.
I can understand formal notices and rules that use the personal infinitive.
I can choose a more colloquial alternative in speech, such as pra gente sair or the subjunctive.

dialogues.title: At the school office
dialogues.context: Seu Roberto has come with his daughter Júlia to enroll her at a school. Teresa, the school secretary, explains the rules.

lines.speaker: Teresa
lines.pt: Bom dia, seu Roberto. Em que posso ajudar?
lines.en: Good morning, Seu Roberto. How can I help?

lines.speaker: Roberto
lines.pt: Bom dia. Viemos fazer a matrícula da Júlia. O que precisamos trazer?
lines.en: Good morning. We came to enroll Júlia. What do we need to bring?

lines.speaker: Teresa
lines.pt: Para vocês fazerem a matrícula hoje, precisam da certidão de nascimento e do histórico escolar.
lines.en: To enroll her today, you need the birth certificate and the school transcript.

lines.speaker: Roberto
lines.pt: Já trouxe tudo. Posso assinar aqui?
lines.en: I've brought everything. Can I sign here?

lines.speaker: Teresa
lines.pt: Pode. Mas antes de assinar, peço que leia o regulamento. É importante os pais conhecerem as regras.
lines.en: You can. But before signing, please read the regulations. It's important for parents to know the rules.

lines.speaker: Roberto
lines.pt: Claro. Tem alguma regra sobre a frequência?
lines.en: Of course. Is there a rule about attendance?

lines.speaker: Teresa
lines.pt: Tem. Os alunos devem ter pelo menos setenta e cinco por cento de presença para serem aprovados.
lines.en: Yes. Students must have at least seventy-five percent attendance in order to pass.

lines.speaker: Júlia
lines.pt: E se eu chegar atrasada de vez em quando?
lines.en: And what if I arrive late once in a while?

lines.speaker: Teresa
lines.pt: O portão fecha às sete e meia. Depois de os alunos chegarem atrasados três vezes, os pais são chamados.
lines.en: The gate closes at seven thirty. After students arrive late three times, the parents are called in.

lines.speaker: Roberto
lines.pt: Entendi. Vou conversar com ela para não chegarmos atrasados.
lines.en: Understood. I'll talk to her so that we don't arrive late.

dialogues.title: Dividing up the work
dialogues.context: Camila, the project manager, meets Diego and Ana to divide the tasks before a Friday deadline. Note how Camila speaks more formally than Diego.

lines.speaker: Camila
lines.pt: Pessoal, para entregarmos o projeto na sexta, cada um precisa cumprir a sua parte.
lines.en: Everyone, for us to deliver the project on Friday, each person needs to do their part.

lines.speaker: Diego
lines.pt: Eu e a Ana ficamos com o relatório. Pra gente terminar hoje, a gente precisa dos dados do cliente.
lines.en: Ana and I will take the report. For us to finish today, we need the client's data.

lines.speaker: Camila
lines.pt: Vou pedir ao pessoal de TI para eles enviarem tudo ainda hoje.
lines.en: I'll ask the IT people to send everything today.

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.pt: Ótimo. Sem eles nos ajudarem, não vamos conseguir terminar no prazo.
lines.en: Great. Without them helping us, we won't manage to finish on time.

lines.speaker: Diego
lines.pt: E a apresentação? É melhor vocês falarem com o cliente, eu fico nervoso.
lines.en: And the presentation? It's better for you two to talk to the client; I get nervous.

lines.speaker: Camila
lines.pt: Tudo bem. Ana e eu fazemos isso. Por não termos avisado o cliente antes, ele ficou chateado.
lines.en: Fine. Ana and I will do it. Because we didn't warn the client earlier, he got upset.

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.pt: Então vamos ligar antes de ele chegar ao escritório, a fim de explicar tudo.
lines.en: Then let's call before he arrives at the office, in order to explain everything.

lines.speaker: Diego
lines.pt: E depois de terminarmos, a gente revisa tudo junto, combinado?
lines.en: And after we finish, we review everything together, agreed?

lines.speaker: Camila
lines.pt: Combinado. Além de cumprirmos o prazo, quero o relatório sem erros.
lines.en: Agreed. Besides meeting the deadline, I want the report without errors.

dialogues.title: Group project at the university
dialogues.context: Lucas and Bia are talking to their professor, Marcelo, about a group project in the corridor of the faculty.

lines.speaker: Lucas
lines.pt: Professor, o senhor disse que o trabalho em grupo vale metade da nota, né?
lines.en: Professor, you said the group project is worth half of the grade, right?

lines.speaker: Professor Marcelo
lines.pt: Isso mesmo. Por isso é importante vocês dividirem as tarefas para ninguém ficar sobrecarregado.
lines.en: Exactly. That is why it's important for you to divide the tasks so nobody gets overloaded.

lines.speaker: Bia
lines.pt: A gente já combinou. Cada um escreve uma parte, e depois de todos terminarem, a gente junta tudo.
lines.en: We've already agreed. Each one writes a part, and after everyone finishes, we put it all together.

lines.speaker: Professor Marcelo
lines.pt: Perfeito. E lembrem que os colegas devem entregar o trabalho até sexta, sem exceção.
lines.en: Perfect. And remember that you must hand in the project by Friday, no exceptions.

lines.speaker: Lucas
lines.pt: E se algum colega faltar no dia da apresentação?
lines.en: And what if a team member is absent on the day of the presentation?

lines.speaker: Professor Marcelo
lines.pt: Ele tem que me avisar antes. Ao faltarem sem avisar, os alunos perdem pontos.
lines.en: He has to tell me beforehand. When students are absent without notice, they lose points.

lines.speaker: Bia
lines.pt: Então vou lembrar o pessoal de me mandarem uma mensagem se tiver algum problema.
lines.en: Then I'll remind everyone to message me if there's any problem.

lines.speaker: Professor Marcelo
lines.pt: Muito bem. Em vez de deixarem tudo pra última hora, comecem hoje mesmo.
lines.en: Very good. Instead of leaving everything for the last minute, start today.

grammar.title: Forming the personal infinitive
grammar.explanation:
The personal infinitive (infinitivo pessoal or flexionado) is an infinitive with person endings, a feature of Portuguese that English, Spanish and French do not have. It is formed by adding endings to the plain infinitive: -es for tu, -mos for nós and -em for eles and vocês. The forms for eu and for ele, ela and você are identical to the plain infinitive, so nothing is added.

The rule is the same for every verb, regular or not, because the endings attach to the infinitive and not to a stem: fazer gives fazermos and fazerem, ir gives irmos and irem, ser gives sermos and serem. For regular verbs these forms look identical to the future subjunctive (quando falarmos, quando falarem), but irregular verbs differ, since the future subjunctive of ser is for while its personal infinitive is sermos.

The tu form (falares) appears only where tu is used with its own verb forms, mainly in some regions of the south and north, and in older texts. Everywhere else you will mostly meet the -mos and -em forms.

grammar.title: When the personal infinitive is needed
grammar.explanation:
The core rule: use the inflected infinitive when the infinitive has its own subject that is different from the subject of the main verb, especially when that subject is plural or is a first person plural. Compare Eles querem sair (same subject, plain infinitive) with É melhor eles saírem or Pedi para eles saírem (the infinitive has its own subject). Eles is a subject of saírem, so it needs the ending.

Notice that the ending helps the listener know who the subject is. In É importante chegarmos cedo there is no pronoun, but -mos tells you that it is about us. With a singular subject, the personal infinitive looks exactly like the plain infinitive: Para ele chegar cedo, acorda às cinco.

Do not use the inflected form after auxiliary and modal verbs with the same subject, where the verb group forms one unit: Eles devem chegar cedo, Eles podem entrar, Eles vão sair. After verbs of perception and causation (ver, ouvir, deixar, mandar) with a noun object you may use either form: Vi os meninos entrar or Vi os meninos entrarem. With a pronoun object, the plain infinitive is standard: Vi-os entrar.

grammar.title: After prepositions: time, reason and purpose
grammar.explanation:
The personal infinitive is most natural after prepositions and prepositional phrases, because it lets you say a whole clause with a prepositional opening. Time: antes de, depois de, ao, até. Purpose: para, a fim de. Reason: por, por causa de. Alternatives: sem, em vez de, além de, apesar de. Example: Antes de chegarmos, ligamos para o cliente; Para terminarmos no prazo, trabalhamos no sábado.

Ao plus an infinitive means upon doing something or when something happens: Ao chegarem, os alunos assinam a lista. When the subject is a pronoun such as ele, ela, eles or elas, careful writing keeps de separate from it: antes de ele chegar, depois de eles saírem. The contracted forms antes dele chegar and depois deles saírem are common in casual speech, but they are considered incorrect in formal writing.

So the pattern is preposition + subject + inflected infinitive. If the subject is the same as the main clause, you may drop it and keep the inflection for emphasis or clarity (Depois de terminarmos, saímos), or use the plain infinitive (Depois de terminar, saí).

grammar.title: Required, optional or colloquial?
grammar.explanation:
Grammars present the personal infinitive as a precise tool, but in real Brazilian speech it is often optional and sometimes avoided. In writing, especially in laws, contracts, school regulations, formal letters and news, you will see it constantly: Os alunos devem informar a secretaria antes de saírem. In speech, people often choose a different structure that avoids the inflection.

Colloquial alternatives: with a gente, use the plain infinitive (Pra gente sair cedo, vamos acordar às cinco); with other subjects, use para que or depois que plus the subjunctive (Pra que eles cheguem cedo..., Depois que eles chegarem...), or just inflect (É melhor vocês irem) which is still perfectly natural. Dropping the ending with a plural subject, as in Pra eles chegar, is common in casual speech but considered incorrect in writing.

A practical rule for a learner: recognize it everywhere, produce it confidently after a preposition with nós, vocês and eles, and remember that if a sentence works fine with a singular subject, the verb will look exactly like the plain infinitive anyway.

culture.title: Formal writing and school life in Brazil
culture.text:
The personal infinitive is a characteristic feature of Portuguese, and Brazilian formal writing uses it heavily. School regulations, workplace memos, contracts and legal texts are full of phrases such as Os alunos devem apresentar o atestado ao retornarem or Pede-se aos moradores para não deixarem objetos no corredor. Reading these texts is the best way to get a feel for the structure, even though in conversation people usually find a lighter way to say the same thing.

School life also explains much of the vocabulary in this unit. Brazilian students must attend at least seventy-five percent of classes to pass the year, which is why the word frequência is so important and why teachers call the roll (fazem a chamada) at the start of class. Enrollment (matrícula) usually takes place in December and January, before the school year starts in February. Universities and companies often ask for group projects (trabalhos em grupo), where dividing tasks fairly is a classic source of complaints.

In the workplace, punctuality is valued but treated with some flexibility, especially outside the big cities where traffic can be unpredictable. Many teams have an informal agreement with the boss (a combinado) about flexible arrival times. Still, in formal notices the tone is polite and firm: Solicitamos a todos que cumpram o horário, or Pedimos a gentileza de chegarem no horário.

paragraphs.pt: Prezados colaboradores, informamos que, a partir de primeiro de março, entram em vigor novas regras de trabalho. Pedimos a todos para lerem este comunicado com atenção.
paragraphs.en: Dear colleagues, we inform you that new work rules take effect on March 1. We ask everyone to read this notice carefully.

paragraphs.pt: Para os funcionários chegarem com mais tranquilidade, o horário de entrada passa a ser flexível, entre oito e dez horas. É necessário, porém, os colegas cumprirem as oito horas diárias.
paragraphs.en: So that employees can arrive more calmly, the start time becomes flexible, between eight and ten o'clock. It is necessary, however, that colleagues complete the eight daily hours.

paragraphs.pt: Antes de saírem de férias, os funcionários devem comunicar a chefia com trinta dias de antecedência. Sem a aprovação do gerente, nenhuma folga será concedida.
paragraphs.en: Before going on vacation, employees must inform management thirty days in advance. Without the manager's approval, no time off will be granted.

paragraphs.pt: As equipes serão responsáveis por dividirem as tarefas de forma justa. Além de entregarem os projetos no prazo, todos devem registrar o andamento do trabalho no sistema.
paragraphs.en: The teams will be responsible for dividing the tasks fairly. Besides delivering projects on time, everyone must record the progress of their work in the system.

paragraphs.pt: Os estagiários, ao chegarem à empresa, devem assinar a lista de presença. Em vez de usarem o celular durante as reuniões, pedimos que façam anotações no caderno.
paragraphs.en: Interns, upon arriving at the company, must sign the attendance sheet. Instead of using their phones during meetings, we ask them to take notes in a notebook.

paragraphs.pt: Caso haja dúvidas, basta os interessados procurarem o departamento de pessoal. Agradecemos a colaboração de todos. Cordialmente, a Diretoria.
paragraphs.en: If there are questions, those concerned only need to contact the personnel department. We thank everyone for their cooperation. Sincerely, the Management.
